threads.title: The Hormuz shock
threads.dek: Iran's near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz is rippling through oil prices, shipping and politics far beyond the Gulf.
threads.why: About a fifth of the world's oil and much of its liquefied gas normally pass through the Strait of Hormuz. Since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in February, Iran has mined and attacked shipping there while a US blockade chokes Iran's own exports, so the strait is shut to most traffic. That one choke point now links tanker crews off Oman, fuel prices in Pakistan and Kenya, gas supplies in Japan and Korea, Qatar's role as mediator and Trump's political fortunes at home.
threads.watch: Whether Qatar's mediation produces a reopening deal, or Washington and Israel resume strikes. Iran says the strait stays shut until its seven conditions are met.

threads.title: Talking while fighting in Ukraine
threads.dek: US-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine have restarted, while the air war on power grids and refineries hits new peaks.
threads.why: For the first time since February, Russia and Ukraine are meeting face to face, with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner shuttling between Kyiv, Moscow and Abu Dhabi and Europe pushing to join. At the same time both sides are firing record numbers of drones: Russia at Ukraine's power stations as winter starts, Ukraine at Russian refineries and Baltic ports. Every strike is also a message to the negotiators, and the talks now reach into US-China-Russia summitry.
threads.watch: The prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi, whether Russia accepts Europe at the next round outside Moscow, whether Kushner's claim that Moscow accepts Article 5-style guarantees holds, and how far Russia's retaliation for the Crimean Bridge strikes goes, including into Poland.

threads.title: The Gulf rearms and realigns
threads.dek: Houthi missiles on Riyadh, a new Saudi-Pakistani-Turkish defence pact and wavering US support are redrawing Gulf security.
threads.why: Saudi Arabia is at war with Yemen's Houthis again, with missiles hitting Riyadh's financial district and airports. Unsure how far Washington will go, Riyadh has built its own coalition: the Mecca defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey, Egyptian promises of support and British jets. These deals tie Pakistan's army and Turkey's arms industry to Gulf wars, and they could outlast this crisis.
threads.watch: Whether the Houthis carry out their threat to hit Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports after the coalition's strike on Hodeidah, whether their offensive through Lahj reaches Aden, and whether Pakistan or Egypt send forces.

threads.title: The Horn of Africa's linked wars
threads.dek: Sudan's civil war, renewed fighting in Ethiopia and an Ethiopia-Eritrea standoff are bleeding into each other.
threads.why: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of letting drones be launched against it from Ethiopian soil; Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut relations after war returned to Tigray; Egypt has built a bloc with Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan against Ethiopia; and the UAE is widely reported to back Sudan's RSF. A strike on a market in disputed Abyei dragged South Sudan in. Each war feeds the others, and together they make the region the world's largest humanitarian crisis.
threads.watch: The army's push from Al-Khuwei toward En Nahud in West Kordofan, drone strikes across the Sudan-Ethiopia border, and any Ethiopian move toward Eritrea's port of Assab.

threads.title: The Sahel's new order
threads.dek: Military juntas, Russia's Africa Corps and jihadist blockades are remaking the Sahel, and the violence is moving toward the coast.
threads.why: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger expelled French and US forces, left ECOWAS and turned to Russia. Jihadists from JNIM and Islamic State now besiege towns and roads across all three, a coup attempt in Niger was put down with Russian help, and Algeria has broken with its old caution by sending troops into Niger. Attacks are spreading into Benin, Togo and Nigeria.
threads.watch: JNIM's blockades around Bamako, Algeria's deployment in Niger, and attacks in northern Benin and Togo.

threads.title: Congo's war turns political
threads.dek: Former president Kabila has joined the M23 rebels in a bid to topple Tshisekedi, as Ebola spreads in the same region.
threads.why: The Rwandan-backed M23 already holds Goma and Bukavu. In October former president Joseph Kabila launched a coalition with it, aimed at toppling President Tshisekedi, turning a regional war into a fight for Kinshasa itself. US-brokered peace deals between Congo and Rwanda have not stopped the fighting, and an Ebola outbreak has passed 5,000 deaths in the same eastern provinces.

threads.title: Washington's war in its own hemisphere
threads.dek: Since capturing Maduro in January, the US has used force across the Caribbean and Latin America, and now talks of Cuba.
threads.why: The US calls its campaign against drug cartels an armed conflict. It has sunk scores of boats, seized Venezuela's president in a raid in January, helped Venezuela strike Colombian guerrillas, and Trump now says he wants to 'get Cuba done'. Governments across the region are choosing sides, from El Salvador sending troops to Haiti to Colombia's new government ending peace talks with armed groups.
threads.watch: Any US move against Cuba, Venezuela's transition, and boat strikes in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.

threads.title: Europe's incumbents under pressure
threads.dek: From Budapest to Brussels, long-serving leaders and coalitions are losing power, majorities or the street.
threads.why: Orbán lost Hungary in April, Vučić conceded defeat in Serbia in October, Czech governing parties were shut out of the Senate, Slovakia's Fico lost his majority, Belgium's government nearly fell over its budget, and Poland's president and prime minister are locked in a constitutional standoff. Behind it are the cost of living, the war next door and anger at entrenched elites, which also drive the protests in France, Germany, Spain and Albania.
threads.watch: Serbia's new government, Fico's survival, France's 17 November protests, and Poland's court crisis.

threads.title: Trump after the midterms
threads.dek: Democrats won both houses of Congress, partly on the Iran war, and the world is watching what a weakened Trump does next.
threads.why: The 3 November midterms gave Democrats the House and the Senate, and Vice President Vance blamed the Iran war. From January, Congress can block funding and investigate. Trump, now questioning results he first accepted, is leaning on foreign policy where he acts alone: Iran, Ukraine talks, a summit with Xi and Putin, threats against Cuba and a permanent base in Poland.
threads.watch: The Shenzhen summit, a decision on new Iran strikes, and the new Congress's first moves in January.

threads.title: Pakistan's war on two fronts
threads.dek: Pakistan is fighting the Taliban government in Afghanistan and insurgents at home, while its army takes on Gulf commitments.
threads.why: Pakistan declared 'open war' on Afghanistan's Taliban in February, accusing it of sheltering the Pakistani Taliban (TTP), whose attacks keep killing police and soldiers in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. At home the government imposed emergency rule on that province and detained Imran Khan's party leaders, and abroad it has signed the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia. China, which has billions invested in Pakistan, is trying to mediate.
threads.watch: Cross-border strikes on Afghanistan, TTP attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and whether Pakistan sends troops to the Gulf.
